full_recipe.procedure:
The following procedure is based on a 1.0 mmol scale of the starting material. 
1. To a round-bottom flask, add tert-butyl (6-(3-(benzyloxy)phenoxy)-1,3-dimethyl-2-oxo-2,3-dihydro-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-5-yl)carbamate (1.0 mmol, 502 mg). 
2. Add dichloromethane (DCM, 8 mL) and stir to dissolve the solid. 
3. Cool the solution to 0 °C using an ice-water bath. 
4. Slowly add trifluoroacetic acid (TFA, 2 mL, 26.1 mmol) dropwise to the stirred solution over 5 minutes. 
5. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature (25 °C). 
6. Stir the reaction for 1-2 hours, monitoring its progress by TLC or LC-MS until the starting material is fully consumed. 
7. Once the reaction is complete, concentrate the mixture under reduced pressure to remove the DCM and excess TFA. 
8. To isolate the free amine, dissolve the residue in ethyl acetate (20 mL) and carefully add saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate solution until gas evolution ceases and the aqueous layer is basic (pH ~8). 
9. Transfer the mixture to a separatory funnel, separate the layers, and extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate (2 x 15 mL). 
10. Combine the organic layers, wash with brine (20 mL), dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. 
11. The crude product can be purified by flash column chromatography on silica gel if necessary.

full_recipe.procedure: To a stirred solution of 5-ethylsulfonyl-6-(7-(trifluoromethyl)imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazin-2-yl)pyridin-3-ol (1.0 mmol, 1.0 eq) in N,N-Dimethylformamide (8.0 mL), cool the mixture to 0 °C using an ice-water bath. Add N-bromosuccinimide (1.1 mmol, 1.1 eq) portion-wise, maintaining the internal temperature below 5 °C. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature (approx. 25 °C). Stir for 1 hour. Monitor the reaction progress by LCMS or TLC. Upon completion, quench the reaction by pouring it into a cold aqueous solution of sodium thiosulfate (10%, 20 mL). Dilute the mixture with water (30 mL) and extract with ethyl acetate (3 x 50 mL). The combined organic layers are washed with water, then with brine, dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filtered, and concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude product is then purified by flash column chromatography on silica gel to yield the brominated product.

full_recipe.procedure: In a round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar, suspend 5-ethylsulfonyl-6-[7-(trifluoromethyl)imidazo[1,2-c]pyrimidin-2-yl]pyridin-3-ol (1.0 eq) and potassium carbonate (2.5 eq) in acetonitrile (10 mL / mmol of substrate). Stir the suspension at room temperature (25 °C). Add 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (1.2 eq) dropwise to the mixture. Continue stirring at room temperature for 2 hours, monitoring the progress of the O-alkylation by LCMS or TLC. Once the starting material is consumed, add N-Bromosuccinimide (1.1 eq) to the reaction mixture in one portion. Continue stirring at room temperature for an additional 2 hours, or until the formation of the final product is complete as indicated by LCMS. Upon completion, quench the reaction by adding water. Extract the aqueous mixture with ethyl acetate (3x). Combine the organic layers, wash with brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. The crude product can be purified by column chromatography on silica gel to afford the target compound.

Dry methanol (c=0.3 mol/l) was added to the test tube. The test tube was placed in a round-bottom flask, atop which was placed a calcium chloride-filled drying tube. The reaction mixture was stirred under air at room temperature for 23 h. The solvent was removed in a membrane pump vacuum at a water bath temperature of 50°C. The remaining residue was treated by column chromatography twice ( silica gel, diethyl ether/acetone=2:1 and dichloromethane/acetone=1:1), and the product was obtained as a white solid having a melting point of 133-135°C. full_recipe.procedure:
Based on a 1.0 mmol scale of the limiting reactant, 6-bromo-3-methyl-3,4-dihydroquinazolin-2(1H)-one.

1. To a sealable pressure tube equipped with a magnetic stirrer bar, add 6-bromo-3-methyl-3,4-dihydroquinazolin-2(1H)-one (269 mg, 1.0 mmol, 1.0 equiv.), (R)-S-methyl-S-phenylsulfoximine (233 mg, 1.5 mmol, 1.5 equiv.), cesium carbonate (717 mg, 2.2 mmol, 2.2 equiv.), XPhos (48 mg, 0.1 mmol, 0.1 equiv.), and Pd₂(dba)₃ (23 mg, 0.025 mmol, 0.025 equiv.).
2. Seal the pressure tube, then evacuate the atmosphere and backfill with argon gas. Repeat this cycle three times to ensure an inert atmosphere.
3. Through the septum, add 5 mL of dry, degassed 1,4-dioxane.
4. Seal the tube tightly and place it in a preheated oil bath at 130 °C.
5. Stir the reaction mixture vigorously for 42 hours. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS if desired.
6. After 42 hours, remove the tube from the oil bath and allow it to cool to room temperature.
7. Dilute the cooled suspension with ethyl acetate and filter the mixture through a pad of Celite (kieselguhr). Wash the filter cake thoroughly with additional ethyl acetate.
8. Combine the filtrates and remove the solvent under reduced pressure.
9. Purify the resulting crude residue by silica gel column chromatography to isolate the final product, CN1Cc2cc(N=[S@](C)(=O)c3ccccc3)ccc2NC1=O.

3. Stir the resulting suspension at room temperature (25 °C).

8. Dissolve the residue in ethyl acetate (50 mL) and transfer to a separatory funnel. Wash the organic layer with water (2 x 25 mL) and then with brine (25 mL).
9. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure to yield the crude product.
10. If necessary, purify the crude product by silica gel column chromatography using a hexane/ethyl acetate gradient to afford the pure product, COC(CSc1ccccc1C(C)(C)C)OC.

full_recipe.procedure:
To a round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar and a reflux condenser under an inert atmosphere (e.g., Nitrogen) add 3-methylpyridin-2-amine (1.0 eq), 2-chloro-6-fluorobenzaldehyde (1.0 eq), 6-isocyano-2,3-dihydrobenzo[b][1,4]dioxine (1.0 eq), and 1,4-dioxane (8 mL). Stir the mixture to dissolve the solids. Carefully add a solution of perchloric acid (0.2 eq). 

**SAFETY WARNING:** Perchloric acid is a strong oxidizer and can form explosive mixtures with organic materials, especially upon heating. Handle with extreme caution behind a blast shield. Using a safer alternative catalyst like zinc chloride, indium chloride, or triflic acid is strongly recommended.

Heat the reaction mixture to 100 °C and stir for 18 hours. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS. Upon completion, cool the reaction to room temperature. Dilute the mixture with ethyl acetate and wash with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the crude residue by flash column chromatography on silica gel to afford the desired product.

full_recipe.procedure:
1. Under an inert atmosphere (e.g., nitrogen or argon), add the lactone (1.0 eq) and toluene (10 mL per mmol of lactone) to a flame-dried, round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar.
2. Add cyclohexylamine (1.2 eq) to the solution.
3. Cool the flask to 0 °C using an ice-water bath.
4. Slowly add trimethylaluminum (1.3 eq, as a 2.0 M solution in toluene) dropwise via syringe over 15-20 minutes. CAUTION: Trimethylaluminum is pyrophoric and reacts violently with protic sources. Methane gas is evolved during the addition.
5. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature (approx. 25 °C).
6. Stir the reaction for 12 hours. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS.
7. Upon completion, cool the reaction mixture back to 0 °C. Slowly and carefully quench the reaction by the dropwise addition of a saturated aqueous solution of Rochelle's salt (potassium sodium tartrate). Stir vigorously for 1-2 hours until the aluminum salts precipitate and the biphasic mixture becomes clear.
8. Transfer the mixture to a separatory funnel and dilute with ethyl acetate. Separate the organic layer.
9. Extract the aqueous layer twice more with ethyl acetate.
10. Combine all organic layers, wash with saturated aqueous sodium chloride (brine), dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
11. Purify the crude residue by flash column chromatography on silica gel to yield the desired hydroxy-amide product.

To a round-bottom flask equipped with a reflux condenser and a magnetic stir bar, add the substrate (1.0 eq), N-bromosuccinimide (1.1 eq), and carbon tetrachloride (to achieve a concentration of approx. 0.05-0.1 M). Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄), filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. The crude product can be purified by flash column chromatography on silica gel.

full_recipe.procedure:
The following procedure is based on a 5.0 mmol scale of the limiting reactant.
1. To a flame-dried round-bottom flask under an inert nitrogen atmosphere, add sodium hydride (0.44 g of 60% dispersion in mineral oil, 11.0 mmol, 2.2 eq) and suspend it in anhydrous N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF, 25 mL).
2. Cool the suspension to 0 °C using an ice-water bath.
3. In a separate flask, dissolve 1,3-dihydro-2H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridin-2-one (0.67 g, 5.0 mmol, 1.0 eq) in anhydrous DMF (15 mL).
4. Add the solution of the pyridinone dropwise to the cold NaH suspension over 10 minutes. Hydrogen gas will evolve. Stir the mixture at 0 °C for 30 minutes, then allow it to warm to room temperature and stir for an additional 30 minutes.
5. Dissolve 1,2-bis(bromomethyl)-4-iodobenzene (1.95 g, 5.0 mmol, 1.0 eq) in anhydrous DMF (10 mL) and add this solution dropwise to the reaction mixture at room temperature.
6. Heat the reaction mixture to 60 °C and stir for 16 hours, or until reaction completion is confirmed by TLC or LC-MS analysis.
7. After completion, cool the mixture to 0 °C and cautiously quench the excess NaH by the slow, dropwise addition of water (10 mL).
8. Dilute the mixture with ethyl acetate (100 mL) and water (50 mL). Separate the layers. Extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate (2 x 50 mL).
9. Combine the organic layers, wash with brine (2 x 50 mL), dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
10. Purify the crude residue by flash column chromatography on silica gel (eluting with a gradient of hexane/ethyl acetate) to yield the desired product. Note: The reaction produces a racemic mixture of the two possible enantiomers.

steps: To a round-bottom flask, add 1-benzyl-N-methylpiperidin-4-amine dihydrochloride (1.0 eq) and 1H-Indazole-6-carboxylic acid (1.0 eq).
Add dichloromethane (DCM) to achieve a concentration of approximately 0.1 M relative to the limiting reactant.
Cool the resulting suspension to 0 °C using an ice-water bath.
Add triethylamine (3.0 eq) dropwise to the stirred mixture. Stir for 10-15 minutes at 0 °C.
Add 1-hydroxybenzotriazole (HOBt, 1.1 eq) followed by EDC.HCl (1.1 eq) to the reaction mixture in portions.
Remove the ice bath and allow the reaction to warm to room temperature (approx. 25 °C).
Stir the reaction mixture for 18 hours. Monitor reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS.
Upon completion, dilute the mixture with additional DCM and transfer to a separatory funnel.
Wash the organic layer sequentially with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) solution, water, and brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), filter, and concentrate the solvent under reduced pressure.
Purify the resulting crude residue by flash column chromatography on silica gel to afford the desired product, N-(1-benzylpiperidin-4-yl)-N-methyl-1H-indazole-6-carboxamide.

The following procedure is based on a 5.0 mmol scale of the limiting reactant, 5-bromo-thiophene-2-carbaldehyde.
1. To a round-bottom flask equipped with a reflux condenser and magnetic stir bar, add 5-bromo-thiophene-2-carbaldehyde (0.96 g, 5.0 mmol, 1.0 eq) and tosylmethyl isocyanide (1.03 g, 5.25 mmol, 1.05 eq).

3. To the resulting solution, add potassium carbonate (0.83 g, 6.0 mmol, 1.2 eq).
4. Heat the reaction mixture to reflux (approximately 65 °C) with vigorous stirring.
5. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC (e.g., eluting with 20% ethyl acetate in hexane). The reaction is expected to be complete within 2-5 hours. Let it reflux for 3 hours.
6. After completion, cool the mixture to room temperature and remove the methanol under reduced pressure.
7. Partition the resulting residue between ethyl acetate (50 mL) and water (50 mL).
8. Separate the layers and wash the organic layer with water (2 x 30 mL) and then brine (30 mL).
9. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous magnesium sulfate or sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate in vacuo.
10. Purify the crude residue by silica gel column chromatography, eluting with a hexane/ethyl acetate gradient (e.g., starting from 5% ethyl acetate in hexane) to afford the pure product, 5-(5-bromothiophen-2-yl)oxazole.

The solution was cooled to 0°C. and dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (417 mg, 2.0 mmol) was added. The reaction mixture was stirred at RT for 12 d. Working up of the mixture was carried out by separating off the urea which had precipitated out and introducing the filtrate into a mixture of saturated NaCl solution (40 ml) and saturated NaHCO₃ solution (10 ml). Still further urea thereby precipitated out and was separated off. 5 M sodium hydroxide solution (4 ml, 20 mmol) was added to the aqueous phase and the mixture was diluted with water (300 ml) and stored at 5°C. for 3 d. 4. Stir the reaction mixture at room temperature for 3 hours. The reaction progress can be monitored by TLC.
5. Upon completion, carefully and slowly pour the reaction mixture into an ice-cooled, vigorously stirred saturated aqueous solution of sodium bicarbonate to quench excess thionyl chloride and neutralize HCl. Gas evolution (CO2, SO2) will occur.
6. Transfer the mixture to a separatory funnel and extract with ethyl acetate (3x volume of toluene used).
7. Combine the organic extracts and wash with saturated brine.
8. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous magnesium sulfate or sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate the solvent under reduced pressure to yield the title compound, 3-(chloro(cyclohexyl)methyl)-2-ethyl-5-[4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]thiophene, which is expected as a solid.

full_recipe.procedure: In a flame-dried round-bottom flask under a nitrogen atmosphere, dissolve 3-chloro-4-nitrobenzaldehyde (1.0 eq, e.g., 1.86 g, 10.0 mmol) and diethyl malonate (1.1 eq, e.g., 1.67 mL, 11.0 mmol) in anhydrous toluene (50 mL). Cool the resulting solution to 0 °C using an ice-water bath. To this stirred solution, add titanium(IV) chloride (1.1 eq, e.g., 1.21 mL, 11.0 mmol) dropwise via syringe over 10 minutes, maintaining the temperature at 0 °C. The mixture will likely develop a deep color. Stir the mixture at 0 °C for an additional 20 minutes. Subsequently, add pyridine (2.4 eq, e.g., 1.93 mL, 24.0 mmol) dropwise over 10 minutes, ensuring the temperature does not rise significantly. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature. Stir at room temperature for 4 hours, monitoring the reaction progress by TLC. Upon completion, pour the reaction mixture into a separatory funnel containing 50 mL of 1 M aqueous HCl. Extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate (3 x 50 mL). Combine the organic layers, wash with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate solution (50 mL) and then brine (50 mL). Dry the organic phase over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. The crude product can be purified by recrystallization from ethanol or by column chromatography on silica gel to afford the desired product, CCOC(=O)C(=Cc1cc(Cl)ccc1[N+](=O)[O-])C(=O)OCC.

1. Under an inert atmosphere (e.g., Argon), add a solution of (1-benzylpiperidin-4-yl)magnesium chloride (1.2 equivalents in THF) to a reaction flask.
2. Cool the solution to 0 °C using an ice-water bath.
3. Dissolve 2,5-dimethoxy-3,4,6-trimethylbenzaldehyde (1.0 equivalent) in anhydrous THF (e.g., in a volume approx. 1/3 of the Grignard solution volume).
4. Add the aldehyde solution dropwise to the stirred Grignard solution over 20-30 minutes, maintaining the temperature at 0 °C.
5. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature.
6. Stir the mixture at room temperature for 2 hours. Monitor reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS.
7. Once the reaction is complete, cool the flask back to 0 °C.
8. Slowly and carefully quench the reaction by adding saturated aqueous ammonium chloride solution until no further effervescence or precipitation is observed.
9. Transfer the mixture to a separatory funnel and extract the product with an organic solvent (e.g., ethyl acetate, 3x). 
10. Combine the organic layers, wash with water and then with brine.
11. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate the solvent under reduced pressure.
12. Purify the resulting crude residue by silica gel column chromatography or crystallization to obtain the final product.

Add potassium carbonate (2.0 eq) to the stirred solution. Equip the flask with a reflux condenser and heat the mixture to reflux (approximately 65 °C). Monitor the reaction progress by thin-layer chromatography (TLC) or liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). After the starting material is consumed (estimated 6 hours), cool the reaction to room temperature. Filter the mixture to remove any insoluble salts and concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure. Redissolve the resulting crude residue in ethyl acetate and wash sequentially with water and brine. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate in vacuo. If necessary, purify the crude product via flash column chromatography on silica gel to afford the desired methyl ester.

full_recipe.procedure: In a dry flask under a nitrogen atmosphere, dissolve methyl 5-methyl-1-(4-methoxyphenyl)-4-((3-propionylphenyl)carbamoyl)-1H-pyrazole-3-carboxylate (1.0 g, 1.95 mmol, 1.0 eq) in anhydrous dichloromethane (20 mL). Cool the solution to 0 °C in an ice-water bath. Add diethylaminosulfur trifluoride (DAST, 0.30 mL, 2.34 mmol, 1.2 eq) dropwise over 5 minutes. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature (approx. 25 °C). Stir for 12 hours. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS. Upon completion, carefully and slowly pour the reaction mixture into a vigorously stirred, ice-cold saturated aqueous solution of sodium bicarbonate (50 mL) in a well-ventilated fume hood. Stir for 30 minutes to ensure complete quenching. Separate the organic layer, and extract the aqueous layer twice with dichloromethane (2x 25 mL). Combine the organic layers, wash with brine (30 mL), dry over anhydrous magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the resulting crude oil by silica gel column chromatography to afford the desired product, methyl 5-methyl-1-(4-methoxyphenyl)-4-{[3-(1,1-difluoropropyl)phenyl]carbamoyl}-1H-pyrazole-3-carboxylate.

full_recipe.procedure:
1. In a round-bottom flask, dissolve the ethyl ester starting material (1.0 eq) in methanol (e.g., 5 mL per mmol of substrate).
2. Add potassium carbonate (1.5 eq) to the solution with stirring.
3. Heat the reaction mixture to 50 °C and stir.
4. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS. The reaction is expected to be complete within 4 hours.
5. Once the starting material is consumed, cool the mixture to room temperature.
6. Carefully neutralize the mixture to pH 7 by adding 1 M aqueous HCl dropwise.
7. Remove the methanol solvent under reduced pressure.
8. Add water and ethyl acetate to the residue and transfer to a separatory funnel.
9. Separate the layers and extract the aqueous layer one more time with ethyl acetate.
10. Combine the organic layers, wash with brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and filter.
11. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure to yield the crude product.
12. Purify the crude methyl ester by silica gel column chromatography or recrystallization as needed.

patent_details: To a suspension of 2-amino-N-benzyloxy-acetamide 2,2,2-trifluoroacetic acid (Intermediate Ab, 59 mg, 0.2 mmol) and 4-bromothiophene-2-carboxaldehyde (38 mg, 0.2 mmol) in acetonitrile (1 mL) was added N,N-diisopropylethylamine (33.0 μL, 0.2 mmol). The white suspension was heated for 2 h at 50°C. during which the suspension turned into a clear solution. The mixture was cooled on an ice-water bath to <5°C. and N,N-diisopropylethylamine (33.0 μL, 0.2 mmol) was added. Subsequently a solution of 2,6-difluorobenzoyl chloride (30 μL, 0.24 mmol) in acetonitrile (0.1 mL) was added dropwise keeping the temperature below 5°C. The temperature of the reaction mixture was allowed to come to room temperature. The mixture was partially diluted with ethyl acetate (5 mL) and water (3 mL) was added slowly. The resulting phases were separated and the water layer was extracted with ethyl acetate (3 mL). The combined organic layers were washed with water (5 mL), 5% NaHCO₃-solution (5 mL), water (5 mL) and brine (5 mL), filtered over a PE filter filled with Na₂SO₄ and concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude residue was purified by column chromatography (heptane to ethyl acetate=0 to 100 v/v %) to afford the title compound (72 mg, 72%) as a white solid.

procedure.details:
The following procedure is based on a 10 mmol scale of L-Leucine.
1. Equip a 100 mL round-bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar, a Dean-Stark trap, and a reflux condenser.
2. To the flask, add L-Leucine (1.31 g, 10 mmol, 1.0 eq), toluene (50 mL), cyclopentanol (7.3 mL, 80 mmol, 8.0 eq), and p-toluenesulfonic acid monohydrate (2.28 g, 12 mmol, 1.2 eq).
3. Heat the reaction mixture to reflux (oil bath temperature ~120 °C, internal temperature ~111 °C) with vigorous stirring.
4. Continue refluxing for 24 hours, monitoring the collection of water in the Dean-Stark trap. The reaction can also be monitored by TLC (e.g., 9:1 DCM/MeOH with ninhydrin stain) for the disappearance of L-Leucine.
5. After the reaction is complete, allow the mixture to cool to room temperature, then place it in an ice bath for 1-2 hours to promote crystallization.
6. Collect the precipitated white solid by vacuum filtration.
7. Wash the solid with cold diethyl ether (2 x 20 mL) to remove any remaining starting materials and solvent.
8. Dry the product under high vacuum to afford cyclopentyl L-leucinate p-toluenesulfonate salt.

Upon completion, the product salt may precipitate from the solution. If a solid forms, it is collected by filtration, washed with a small amount of cold ethyl acetate or diethyl ether, and dried under vacuum. If the product remains in solution, the solvent is removed under reduced pressure. The resulting residue is triturated with diethyl ether to induce crystallization, and the solid product is collected by filtration and dried under vacuum to yield the desired cyclopentyl leucinate tosylate salt.

The following procedure is based on a 10 mmol scale of thioanisole.
1. To a dry 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar and a reflux condenser, add succinic anhydride (1.10 g, 11 mmol, 1.1 eq) and Indium(III) triflate (6.18 g, 11 mmol, 1.1 eq) under a nitrogen atmosphere.
2. Add 1,2-dichloroethane (50 mL) to the flask.
3. Stir the suspension and add thioanisole (1.17 mL, 1.24 g, 10 mmol, 1.0 eq) dropwise at room temperature.
4. Heat the reaction mixture to 60 °C and stir for 12 hours. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS.
5. After completion (consumption of thioanisole), cool the mixture to 0 °C in an ice bath.
6. Slowly quench the reaction by adding 2 M HCl aqueous solution (50 mL). Gas evolution may occur.
7. Stir the biphasic mixture vigorously for 30 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a separatory funnel and separate the layers.
8. Extract the aqueous layer with dichloromethane (2 x 30 mL).
9. Combine all organic layers, wash with water (50 mL), then with brine (50 mL).
10. Dry the organic phase over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄), filter, and concentrate the solvent under reduced pressure to obtain the crude product.
11. The crude solid, 4-(4-(methylthio)phenyl)-4-oxobutanoic acid, can be purified by recrystallization from a suitable solvent system (e.g., toluene/heptane) or by flash column chromatography on silica gel.

The reaction is performed in two sequential steps.

Step 1: Nitro Group Reduction
1. To a flask, add 4-(3,5-dimethoxy-6-nitropyrazin-2-yl)piperazin-2-one (1.0 eq) and Methanol (10 mL per mmol of substrate).
2. Carefully add 10% Palladium on carbon (0.1 eq by weight).
3. Purge the flask with hydrogen gas and stir the mixture under a hydrogen atmosphere (balloon or ~1 atm) at room temperature.
4. Monitor the reaction by TLC or LCMS until the starting material is fully consumed (typically 4-12 hours).
5. Once complete, carefully filter the reaction mixture through a pad of Celite to remove the palladium catalyst, washing the pad with additional Methanol.
6. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure to yield the crude amine, 4-(6-amino-3,5-dimethoxypyrazin-2-yl)piperazin-2-one, which can often be used in the next step without further purification.

Step 2: Amide Coupling
1. In a separate dry flask under an inert atmosphere (e.g., Nitrogen), suspend 5-bromo-1,3-thiazole-2-carboxylic acid (1.1 eq) in anhydrous Dichloromethane (5 mL per mmol).
2. Cool the suspension to 0 °C using an ice bath.
3. Add Oxalyl chloride (1.2 eq) dropwise, followed by a catalytic amount of DMF (1 drop).
4. Stir the mixture at 0 °C for 30 minutes, then allow it to warm to room temperature and stir for an additional 1 hour, or until gas evolution ceases.
5. In another flask, dissolve the crude amine from Step 1 in anhydrous Dichloromethane (5 mL per mmol) and add Triethylamine (3.0 eq).
6. Cool this amine solution to 0 °C.
7. Add the freshly prepared acyl chloride solution from step 2.4 dropwise to the cooled amine solution.
8. Stir the reaction mixture at 0 °C for 30 minutes, then allow it to warm to room temperature and stir for 2-4 hours, monitoring by TLC or LCMS.
9. Upon completion, quench the reaction by adding water. Separate the organic layer, and extract the aqueous layer with Dichloromethane.
10. Combine the organic layers, wash with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
11. Purify the crude residue by flash column chromatography on silica gel to afford the final product.

The following procedure is based on a 1.0 mmol scale of the starting aldehyde.
1. To a 50 mL round-bottomed flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar, add the reactant aldehyde (277 mg, 1.0 mmol), 2-methyl-2-butene (0.53 mL, 5.0 mmol), and tert-butanol (8.0 mL). Stir at room temperature until all solids dissolve.
2. In a separate beaker, prepare the oxidant solution by dissolving sodium chlorite (tech. grade, 80%, 169 mg, 1.5 mmol) and sodium dihydrogen phosphate monohydrate (207 mg, 1.5 mmol) in water (2.0 mL).
3. Cool the flask containing the aldehyde solution to 0 °C using an ice-water bath.
4. Add the aqueous oxidant solution dropwise to the stirred aldehyde solution over 15 minutes. A yellow color may develop.
5. After the addition is complete, remove the ice bath and allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature (approx. 25 °C). Stir for 2 hours.
6. Monitor the reaction progress by TLC (e.g., using 3:1 hexanes:ethyl acetate), checking for the disappearance of the starting aldehyde.
7. Upon completion, cool the mixture in an ice bath and cautiously quench any excess oxidant by adding a saturated aqueous solution of sodium sulfite (Na2SO3) dropwise until the yellow color disappears.
8. Acidify the mixture to pH 2-3 by adding 1M HCl. 
9. Transfer the mixture to a separatory funnel and extract the product with ethyl acetate (3 x 20 mL).
10. Combine the organic layers, wash with brine (20 mL), dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), and filter.
11. Concentrate the solvent under reduced pressure to yield the crude carboxylic acid product, which can be further purified by recrystallization or silica gel column chromatography if necessary.

Stir for 4 hours, monitoring the reaction progress by TLC or LC-MS until the starting material is fully consumed. After completion, cool the mixture to room temperature and concentrate it under reduced pressure to remove the methanol. Partition the residue between ethyl acetate and water. Separate the layers and wash the organic layer with saturated aqueous sodium chloride (brine). Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
